title: Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence
summary: In the summer of 1956 a study of two months and about ten people was planned at Dartmouth College in Hanover, New Hampshire, following an August 1955 proposal by McCarthy, Minsky, Rochester and Shannon. The proposal's basic conjecture was that every aspect of learning, and any other feature of intelligence, could be described precisely enough for a machine to simulate it.

uncertainty.note: Exact days of the summer 1956 study are not given on the opened pages; the proposal itself is dated 31 August 1955.

as_recorded.value: The original proposal was dated August 31, 1955.

importance.justification: The proposal for the 1956 Dartmouth study is the primary document for the event, and sets out the conjecture that machines could simulate intelligence.
